summary: Establishes normative script policy: POSIX shell by default; PowerShell only when Windows support is explicit
migration_impact: Authoring policy is POSIX shell by default and PowerShell only when Windows support is explicit. import-payload and bootstrap --apply still copy every manifest script, including .ps1. Leave those files in place: validate_plate_repo.sh fails without scripts/gif-from-video.ps1, and a *.ps1 glob would also delete adopter-owned scripts. Import filtering and platform-aware validation are #1019.
migration_guidance: 1. Review platform stance: default projects (no explicit Windows support) author .sh only; explicit Windows support = dual-stack (.sh + .ps1); Windows-only = .ps1 only.

2. Scaffold still copies .ps1. Do not delete scripts/*.ps1 or scripts/plate/*.ps1. The template validator requires scripts/gif-from-video.ps1, and template CI runs it on every pull request. A glob also removes adopter-owned PowerShell, including when PLATE helpers are namespaced under scripts/plate/.
3. When creating new scripts, check declared platform support first. Do not wait for an explicit POSIX statement: no Windows declaration means .sh only.
4. Platform support must come from human-stated project intent (SPEC.md, .plate config, onboarding answers, explicit instruction) — never inferred from developer OS or CI platform.

5. Existing dual-stack repositories (PLATE itself, adopters that declared Windows support) keep both .sh and .ps1. #1019 covers import filtering, validation that follows the declared platform, and any later removal limited to PLATE-owned basenames.
agent_notes: When authoring or modifying scripts: (1) Check if the project explicitly declares Windows support via SPEC.md, .plate config, or bootstrap answers. (2) Default projects (no explicit Windows support) = author .sh only. (3) Windows-supported (explicit) = ship both .sh (primary) and .ps1 (equivalent behavior). (4) Windows-only (explicit) = .ps1 only. Never infer platform support from developer laptop OS, Windows dependencies, or CI choices. import-payload and bootstrap still install the payload's .ps1 files. Tell adopters to leave them in place: validate_plate_repo.sh fails without scripts/gif-from-video.ps1, and a *.ps1 glob deletes adopter-owned scripts. Filtering and platform-aware validation are #1019.
